issues.t: Timing chain tensioner can fail
issues.sym: A short rattle on cold start, a check engine light, rough running, or an engine that suddenly dies and will not restart.
issues.why: The original tensioner can wear and release, letting the timing chain slip. If the chain jumps, valves hit pistons and the engine is badly damaged.
issues.next: If you hear a start-up rattle, stop driving and have a shop check which tensioner is fitted. Replace an early-style one before it fails.

issues.t: Intake manifold fails early
issues.sym: Check engine light, rough idle, hesitation or reduced power.
issues.why: The plastic intake manifold and its internal flap mechanism do not hold up to repeated heat cycles and can crack or stick.
issues.next: Have the fault codes read and the manifold inspected. It is safe for short trips, but fix it before it causes misfires.

issues.t: Water pump housing cracks and leaks coolant
issues.sym: Low coolant warning, sweet smell, drips at the front of the engine, or the temperature gauge rising.
issues.why: The water pump and thermostat sit in a plastic housing that cracks or warps with heat. Some owners have had the pump replaced more than once.
issues.next: Top up the coolant and have the leak repaired soon. Stop driving if the engine starts to overheat, since that can ruin it.

issues.t: Ignition coils fail and cause misfires or stalling
issues.sym: Shaking at idle, hesitation, a flashing check engine light, or the engine cutting out.
issues.why: The coil that fires each spark plug can fail with heat and age, leaving that cylinder dead.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Have the misfire codes read and replace the failed coil, ideally with fresh spark plugs. If the check engine light flashes, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off.

issues.t: Engine speed can rise unexpectedly
issues.sym: The engine revs up by itself, or the vehicle surges, without more pressure on the gas pedal.
issues.why: A fault in the engine computer software on 2009 models could raise engine speed without driver input. A recall updates the software.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 08V-235. If it surges, brake firmly, shift to neutral and stop safely.

issues.t: Exterior light fuse holder can melt
issues.sym: Some headlights or taillights stop working, sometimes with a hot plastic smell from the fuse box.
issues.why: The fuse for the exterior lights can overheat in its holder and melt, cutting power to part of the lighting.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check the VIN for recall 13V-569. Do not drive at night with lights out, and have the fuse box inspected.

issues.t: Engine can stall on winter-blend fuel
issues.sym: The engine stumbles or stalls, mostly in cold weather or after a fill-up, and may be hard to restart.
issues.why: Winter gasoline can form vapor bubbles in the fuel system, starving the engine. A recall raises fuel pump pressure through a software update.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check the VIN for recall 14V-441 and have it completed, since a stall in traffic is a safety risk.

issues.t: Steering wheel clock spring can tear and disable the airbag
issues.sym: Airbag warning light on, sometimes with the horn or steering wheel buttons not working.
issues.why: Debris can get into the coiled cable behind the steering wheel and tear it, cutting power to the driver airbag.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 15V-483. An airbag light means the driver airbag may not fire, so have it repaired promptly.

issues.t: Seat-mounted side airbag inflator can rupture
issues.sym: No symptom before a crash. In a crash the side airbag in the seat may not protect properly.
issues.why: Inflators in the seat side airbags on vehicles built during one week in January 2015 could burst when deploying.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 16V-045 and have the side airbag modules replaced if it is open.

issues.t: Airbag control module can fail
issues.sym: Airbag warning light on. The airbags may not work in a crash, or could go off without one.
issues.why: A capacitor inside the airbag control module can fail. The recall installs software and replaces the module when needed.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 19V-535 and have it done soon. Do not ignore an airbag light.

issues.t: Rear child door locks can switch off
issues.sym: A rear door that should be child-locked opens from the inside.
issues.why: The child lock mechanism in the rear door latches can disengage by itself on some 2016 vehicles.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 16V-464. Test the child locks regularly if children ride in the back.

issues.t: Front ball joint nut may be loose
issues.sym: Clunking from a front corner, vague steering, or in the worst case a front wheel that folds outward.
issues.why: The nut holding the lower ball joint may not have been tightened properly at the factory on some 2018 vehicles.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 18V-324. If it is open, do not drive the vehicle until the nut has been replaced.

issues.t: Sunroof ambient lighting can short circuit
issues.sym: Burn marks or a hot smell around the panoramic sunroof frame, or the roof light strip not working.
issues.why: Moisture can reach the LED module for the sunroof ambient lighting and cause a short, which can scorch the headliner or start a fire.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 18V-467. If you smell burning near the roof, stop and have it inspected.

issues.t: Steering rack mounting bolt can corrode and break
issues.sym: A knock through the steering wheel, steering that feels loose or off-center.
issues.why: A bolt that holds the steering rack to the subframe can rust and snap. The recall replaces the right-side bolt.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 26V-590 and have steering looseness inspected right away.

issues.t: Rear coil springs can break
issues.sym: A bang or clunk from the rear, one rear corner sitting low, or a rear tire being rubbed or punctured.
issues.why: Some rear springs were made incorrectly and can fracture. A broken end can damage the tire.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 19V-188. If a rear corner is sagging, have it inspected before driving at speed.

issues.t: Panoramic sunroof leaks water into the cabin
issues.sym: Wet headliner, water dripping from the roof console or pillars, damp carpets or a musty smell after rain.
issues.why: The drains and frame seals of the large sunroof can clog or come loose, so water runs inside instead of out. Owners filed a class action over it.
issues.next: Have the drains cleared and tested, and ask the dealer about extended sunroof coverage. Dry the interior quickly to protect wiring.

issues.t: Rear hatch spoiler can come loose
issues.sym: A rattling or visibly loose spoiler at the top of the rear hatch.
issues.why: The spoiler may not be attached firmly enough and could detach while driving, which is a hazard for traffic behind.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 22V-226 and have the spoiler replaced if it is open.

issues.t: Front seat frame may be poorly welded
issues.sym: A front seatback that feels loose or creaks. In a crash it may not hold.
issues.why: On some 2020 vehicles the front seat frame and backrest adjuster were not welded correctly.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 20V-505 and have the seat frames inspected.

issues.t: Rear suspension knuckles can crack
issues.sym: Clunking from the rear, the vehicle feeling unstable, or a rear wheel that looks tilted.
issues.why: The rear knuckles on some vehicles can corrode, crack and break, which can cause sudden loss of control.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 22V-176. If the rear feels loose, stop driving and have it towed in.

issues.t: Brake pipe nut can be loose and leak fluid
issues.sym: A soft or sinking brake pedal, brake warning light, or fluid drips under the vehicle.
issues.why: A brake pipe fitting may not have been tightened fully at the factory, letting brake fluid escape.
issues.next: If the brake pedal sinks, feels soft or goes closer to the floor, or a red brake warning comes on, slow down gently, use a lower gear, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on: call for a tow. Check the VIN for recall 21V-853. If the pedal feels soft, do not drive it; have it towed.

issues.t: Backup camera image may not appear
issues.sym: A black, frozen or missing picture on the screen when shifting into reverse.
issues.why: Software and memory faults in the infotainment unit or camera control unit can stop the image from loading at startup.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recalls 20V-716, 22V-514, 25V-082 and 26V-321. Until fixed, reverse using mirrors and a shoulder check.

issues.t: Front passenger airbag can be switched off by a wiring fault
issues.sym: Airbag warning light or passenger airbag off light showing with an adult in the seat.
issues.why: A wiring fault in the seat occupant detection system can disable the front passenger airbag.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 25V-854. Keep the front passenger seat empty until the harness is repaired.

issues.t: Rear tie rod bolt may be loose
issues.sym: A knock from the rear, the vehicle wandering, or uneven rear tire wear.
issues.why: A bolt on the rear axle tie rod may not have been tightened properly, which lets the rear wheel alignment move.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 25V-526 and have rear-end noises inspected right away.

issues.t: Wrong driver airbag may be fitted
issues.sym: Nothing you can see from the driver seat; the airbag in the steering wheel may not be the one built for US rules.
issues.why: Some Tiguan Limited models left the factory with a driver airbag made for another market, so it may not protect as intended in a crash.
issues.next: Have the free recall repair done, which replaces the steering wheel and driver airbag.

issues.t: Rear shock absorber mount can break away
issues.sym: Clunking or banging from the rear over bumps, and in a bad case the rear of the car feels loose or sags on one side.
issues.why: A weld at the lower loop of the rear shock absorber may be weak and can let the shock separate from its mount.
issues.next: Stop driving over rough roads and have the free recall inspection done, since a detached shock affects how the car handles.

issues.t: Front passenger airbag may tear when it deploys
issues.sym: No warning in normal driving; the passenger airbag may rip instead of inflating properly in a crash.
issues.why: The passenger airbag cushion may have been made with a fault that lets it tear as it fills.
issues.next: Have the free recall replacement done before carrying a front passenger regularly.

issues.t: Front seat belt webbing can tear in a crash
issues.sym: Nothing to feel day to day; the belt looks and latches normally.
issues.why: The front seat belt webbing may have been weakened in manufacturing and can tear under crash loads.
issues.next: Have the free recall inspection done, and have the belt replaced if it is one of the affected ones.

issues.t: Tire pressure warning may not come on
issues.sym: No low tire warning even when every tire is well below the right pressure, because the system compares the wheels with each other.
issues.why: The tire pressure monitor software may miss the case where all four tires lose pressure at the same rate.
issues.next: Have the software update done and check your tire pressures with a gauge each month. It may be covered.

issues.t: Body control module can reset and stall the engine
issues.sym: The engine can cut out while driving, and lights, warning lamps or the rear camera can go dead at the same time.
issues.why: The body control module software can reset itself, dropping the signals the rest of the car depends on.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Have the free recall software update done promptly, since a stall in traffic is a safety risk.

issues.t: Carbon builds up on the intake valves
issues.sym: As the miles pile up the engine idles rough, hesitates or shudders when you accelerate, and can set a misfire code; fuel economy slips too.
issues.why: Fuel is injected straight into the cylinder on this turbo four, so nothing rinses the oil mist and soot off the back of the intake valves and the deposits choke the airflow.
issues.next: Have the intake valves inspected if it runs rough; they are cleaned by hand, and on a high-mileage car expect it to need doing again later.

issues.t: Crankcase breather valve tears and upsets the idle
issues.sym: Check engine light with a lean running or crankcase pressure code, a rough or hunting idle, a whistling or sucking noise from the top of the engine, and sometimes fresh oil seepage.
issues.why: The thin plastic diaphragm in the crankcase breather housing (the PCV and oil separator unit) splits, so the engine draws air it has not measured and crankcase pressure goes the wrong way.
issues.next: Get it replaced rather than living with it - wrong crankcase pressure pushes oil past seals and turns into bigger oil leaks.

issues.t: Turbocharger and wastegate wear out early
issues.sym: A rattle or chatter from the turbo area at light throttle and low speed, then weak acceleration, a boost-related warning light or a puff of smoke in the worst cases.
issues.why: The wastegate linkage in the turbo housing wears loose and the turbo itself is hard on oil, so neglected oil changes shorten its life further.
issues.next: Have the turbo and its wastegate checked when the rattle starts; keeping to short oil change intervals with the right oil is the best protection.
